# zlar2v

> Applies a vector of complex plane rotations with real cosines from both sides to a sequence of 2-by-2 complex Hermitian matrices.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlar2v from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zlar2v';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlar2v( N, x, strideX, y, strideY, z, strideZ, c, strideC, s, strideS ) → Complex128Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of plane rotations to apply |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incx</sub> | **in/out** · First input array (elements assumed real) |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | `x` stride length (in complex elements) |
| `y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incx</sub> | **in/out** · Second input array (elements assumed real) |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | `y` stride length (in complex elements) |
| `z` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incx</sub> | **in/out** · Third input array (complex) |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | `z` stride length (in complex elements) |
| `c` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incc</sub> | Array of cosines of the plane rotations (real) |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | `c` stride length |
| `s` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incc</sub> | Array of sines of the plane rotations (complex) |
| ↳ `strideS` | `integer` | `s` stride length (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The number of plane rotations to be applied.
- `x`: The vector x; the elements of x are assumed to be real.
- `y`: The vector y; the elements of y are assumed to be real.
- `z`: The vector z.
- `c`: The cosines of the plane rotations.
- `s`: The sines of the plane rotations.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlar2v.ndarray(
    N,
    x, strideX, offsetX,
    y, strideY, offsetY,
    z, strideZ, offsetZ,
    c, strideC, offsetC,
    s, strideS, offsetS
) → Complex128Array
```

Apply a vector of complex plane rotations with real cosines from both sides to a sequence of 2-by-2 complex Hermitian matrices.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incx</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride length for `x` |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `x` |
| `y` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incx</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | Stride length for `y` |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `y` |
| `z` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incx</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideZ` | `integer` | Stride length for `z` |
| ↳ `offsetZ` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `z` |
| `c` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incc</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideC` | `integer` | Stride length for `c` |
| ↳ `offsetC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `c` |
| `s` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length 1 + (N - 1) * incc</sub> | Output array |
| ↳ `strideS` | `integer` | Stride length for `s` |
| ↳ `offsetS` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `s` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The number of plane rotations to be applied.
- `x`: The vector x; the elements of x are assumed to be real.
- `y`: The vector y; the elements of y are assumed to be real.
- `z`: The vector z.
- `c`: The cosines of the plane rotations.
- `s`: The sines of the plane rotations.

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128Array`: `z`

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zlar2v from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/zlar2v';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const x = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
const y = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
const z = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
const c = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const s = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N, -10, 10, opts ) );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = zlar2v( N, x, 1, y, 1, z, 1, c, 1, s, 1 );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = zlar2v.ndarray( N, x, 1, 0, y, 1, 0, z, 1, 0, c, 1, 0, s, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLAR2V`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLAR2V applies a vector of complex plane rotations with real cosines from both sides to a sequence of 2-by-2 complex Hermitian matrices, defined by the elements of the vectors x, y and z. For $i = 1$,2,...,n

$$
\begin{pmatrix} x(i) & z(i) \\ \overline{z(i)} & y(i) \end{pmatrix} :=
$$

$$
\begin{pmatrix} c(i) & \overline{s(i)} \\ -s(i) & c(i) \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} x(i) & z(i) \\ \overline{z(i)} & y(i) \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} c(i) & -\overline{s(i)} \\ s(i) & c(i) \end{pmatrix}
$$

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
